A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text and Appendices A–D are readable, and the equations, figures and experimental material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical experiments on six model families, including theoretical-error comparisons, cross-subspace evaluation, Green's-function extraction, repeated runs and grid-size analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original PINN, physics-informed DeepONet, noisy-data, 2D Poisson and biharmonic results.

M1.justification: The proposed cross-subspace evaluation procedure and Green's-function extraction through one-hot inputs remain unchanged. The newly described PINN and physics-informed DeepONet losses belong to added comparison models, rather than revisions to the proposed diagnostic method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates noiseless 1D Poisson data. v2 retains this coverage and adds noise-corrupted Poisson data, 2D Poisson polynomial/sine datasets, and 1D biharmonic polynomial/sine/cosine datasets (Figures 7–8). These extend measurement conditions, spatial dimensionality and equation coverage.

E2.justification: The six original model families are retained, while v2 adds PINN inverse parameter learning, compared with finite-difference fitting (Section 4.2, Figure 3), and physics-informed DeepONet cross-subspace evaluation alongside the original DeepONet (Figure 6). v1 explicitly excluded physics-informed-loss methods.

E3.justification: New designs include single-solution PINN inverse fits, Gaussian perturbations of both forcing and solution training data, and the 18-by-18 and 24-by-24 comparisons in Figure 8. The original 25-dataset, Ngrid=22 protocol remains. Appendix B now states weight decay 0.01 for all models; v1 prose advocated removing it, although its tables already listed 0.01. Both main texts specify no linear-model regularization, so an actual regularization change or rerun is unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds a measurement-noise robustness analysis asking whether noise obscures the generalization boundaries (Figure 7). Existing grid/order sensitivity analyses and Green's-function inspection cases remain. The addition is limited to the reported noise scenario, without a noise-level sensitivity sweep.

E5.justification: Both appendices report five-run means with min–max ranges. The new PINN plot uses the same five-run mean/min–max practice. No different uncertainty estimator, significance test or increase in repetitions is documented.

E6.justification: All original plotted results are retained. v2 adds PINN parameter errors, physics-informed DeepONet errors reported near 10^-6, noisy-data results with a reported minimum near 10^-9 versus the clean reference near 10^-20, and 2D Poisson/biharmonic generalization patterns (Figures 3 and 6–8). These are additional experimental findings, rather than improved scores for the original comparisons.

T1.justification: The two principal theorems and their proofs are substantially retained. However, v1 Appendix A.4's loose Frobenius-error bound and proof are removed. The remaining error-estimation section changes its expression from ||W0 - AUDV^T||_F in v1 Equation 46 to ||W0 - AUU^T||_F in v2 Equation 47, which is a mathematical revision rather than renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and benchmark recommendation broaden from the 1D Poisson problem to linear differential equations. A fifth contribution and the revised conclusion assert that PINNs and physics-informed DeepONets also exhibit the identified failures, replacing v1's explicit exclusion of these methods. The central subspace, interpretability and cross-validation contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that physics-informed losses do not remove the subspace limitation, noise raises the error floor without erasing boundaries, and 2D generalization occurs independently along each spatial direction. It also removes the dedicated limitations discussion, including the call for real-world validation, and Appendix D's caveat about variable or unknown grid spacing.

D1.justification: v2 removes the SymPy/root-form data-generation recipe, sampling distributions, tuning rationale, finite-difference CPU/float64 specification, runtime estimates and statement that supplementary replication scripts are provided. Most hyperparameters survive as prose replacing Tables 1–5. It newly identifies PyTorch for final runs and DeepXDE for the added models. These substantially change reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to the underlying implementation or actual code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sakarvadia et al. (2025) on spatial-resolution generalization failures and Wang et al. (2021) on physics-informed DeepONets. It removes world-model/robotics and transformer-regression discussions and associated citations, while retaining the central positioning around Green's functions and scientific-ML generalization.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background and numerous experimental passages are extensively condensed or rewritten. Appendix exposition is abridged and reorganized, the limitations paragraph disappears, and an Impact Statement and acknowledgment placeholder appear. This is substantial language and structural editing beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 introduces Figures 3, 6, 7 and 8, consolidates v1 Figures 7–12 into the smaller six-panel Figure 11, and replaces five hyperparameter tables with prose. Existing figures are relocated or resized and several captions are rewritten, substantially changing the visual organization while preserving the original plotted data.

improvement.justification: The added physics-informed, noisy-data and additional-equation experiments address v1's explicit exclusions and narrow empirical scope, strengthening support for the central generalization diagnosis. The gain is moderated by deleted data-generation and replication details, unspecified settings such as noise magnitude, and reduced limitations discussion. Overall, the evidence is broader, but the accompanying transparency losses keep the improvement modest.
